For $\SU(2)$ Wilson lattice gauge theory in four dimensions, consider the infinite-volume limits of periodic states along boxes of side $2^k$. We prove that, along every sequence of couplings $\beta\to\infty$ and of such states, every subsequential limit, in finite-dimensional distributions, of the rescaled curvature field is a free lattice Maxwell field in three independent colours plus an independent random constant. Consequently the normalized correlation of rescaled plaquette energies at time separation $n$ has limit inferior at least $(G(n)/G(0))^2$, with $G$ the free field-strength correlation, and the mass gap of the transfer matrix in lattice units tends to zero or is zero. This is an upper bound and does not address whether the gap is positive. We also record a conditional reduction of the continuum problem to five lattice hypotheses, H0 to H4, of which two are proved; four routes to the principal one, each failing at a stated step, and an argument by exclusion that fails; and six properties shared with $\U(1)$ and $\Z_2$ lattice gauge theories that therefore cannot prove a gap. The paper was written and checked by sessions of artificial-intelligence systems and has not been reviewed by a mathematician.

Other working groups of the same research program, whose sessions state their system as OpenAI Codex, report the following in the program's coordination record. One group reports $m(\beta,\mu)\le C\beta^{-1/8}$ in lattice steps for every even-periodic limit state, and, for each fixed $M$, a gauge-invariant subspace of dimension at least $M$ with energies strictly between zero and $C_M\beta^{-1/8}$ \cite[comment 7102141403]{RepoThread}; the files are~\cite{RepoC4}. A second group reports linearly independent magnetic readings in an energy band between two fixed multiples of $1/R$, $R=\lfloor c\beta^{1/8}\rfloor$ \cite[comment 7102153452]{RepoThread}; the files are~\cite{RepoB4}. The first report, if correct, implies the last sentence of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} with a rate. A third group reports that, under the limit specification and dyadic moment bounds of Section~\ref{sec:proof}, the random constant background of Lemma~\ref{pf:lem-R} vanishes, which would turn the inequality of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} into an equality for every fixed lag \cite[comment 7102652403]{RepoThread}; this is reported, not proved here. A fourth group reports, for the single-plaquette energy itself, that the connected covariance differs from $\tfrac32G(n,z)^2$ by at most $C\beta^{-1/8}$ in every even-periodic limit state, uniformly in the time lag $n$ and for spatial offsets $|z|_1\le\beta^{1/4}$ \cite[comment 7103151190]{RepoThread}, and the record of these groups now carries the bound $C\beta^{-1/7}$ for the gap \cite[comment 7103054156]{RepoThread}. If correct, these reports contain Theorem~\ref{thm:main} with equality and a rate, and Theorem~\ref{thm:main} is then a weaker statement with a different proof. Neither the author nor the sessions that wrote this paper have read those proofs.

Every statement and proof in this paper was written by sessions of one artificial-intelligence model family (Claude, Anthropic), working as a director with subordinate workers, at the direction of the author, who is accountable for the paper. Each proof was then attacked by other sessions of the same family. Agreement among them is not independent review. Sessions of a second model lineage (OpenAI Codex) checked parts of Section~\ref{sec:proof}: Lemma~\ref{pf:lem-R} and the Wick inequality that follows it, by two groups with different arguments \cite[comments 7102490558, 7102590992]{RepoThread}; the asymptotics of $G$, by one \cite[comment 7102490558]{RepoThread}; and the arithmetic of the tail constant $D^*$, by one \cite[comment 7102590992]{RepoThread}. They did not check the identification of the limit of the Wilson measures (Theorem~\ref{pf:thm-L3} and Proposition~\ref{pf:prop-L4}). No mathematician has read the paper. It should be read as a claim awaiting review.

The statements, proofs, programs and text were produced by sessions of one model family, Claude (Anthropic). One session acted as director. It wrote the reduction of Section~\ref{sec:reduction} in its first form, chose the routes of Section~\ref{sec:routes}, and assembled the paper. Subordinate sessions, started by the director as separate processes and each with subordinate sessions of its own, did the following: \emph{builders} wrote the proofs of Theorems~\ref{thm:main}, \ref{thm:reduction} and~\ref{thm:conditional} and the arguments of Sections~\ref{sec:routes}--\ref{sec:CE}; \emph{challengers}, given only the text under attack, tried to break each of them with their own programs; \emph{formalizers} wrote the Lean files of Section~\ref{sec:lean}; \emph{readers} located statements in the literature. Every session shares its model family with the director. Their agreement reduces the exposure to error. It is not independent review.

No mathematician has read the paper. The director session did not read the proofs line by line; it read the statements, the challengers' reports and the tests. The sources cited for attribution were read by reader sessions, several of them only as abstracts; Section~\ref{sec:routes} says so where it matters. The reconstruction theorem used in Theorem~\ref{thm:conditional} was read in~\cite{KQR21}, not in~\cite{OS73,OS75}. The proofs do not depend on any cited result except that reconstruction theorem.
